note: Issue 394, commanders.md section 8, SPEC section 8.6: I stand before the enemy - do I press on? A commander in the field with an enemy in reach asks what the PC wants, and the reply argues with him: it moves the weights of his next deliberation and never his company (Seam B). Unskippable by the director's own example (the-director.md section 2): a man in the field facing an enemy wants orders, and there is no deliberation about whether to trouble the Crown with that. Commanders care about no measures today, so a skippable letter from one would never clear his threshold. Placeholder prose.

body.text: We are in the field near {param:near}, {param:men} of us, and there are {param:enemies} bodies of men within a few days' march who would fight us if they could.
I shall do what I judge best, as I must. I should rather do it knowing what you want.
Your letter will be a month on the road. Whatever you write, write it plainly.

options.text: and a great deal rests on what you do
and I had hoped for better news

steps.prompt: What the Crown would have him do

options.label: press on and fall on them
options.text: Press on. Fall on them before they have the chance to choose the ground.

options.label: hold where he stands
options.text: Hold where you are and let them come to you.

options.label: fall back to the town that feeds him
options.text: Fall back to the town that feeds you. I would rather have your men than the ground.

options.label: stand the men down
options.text: Stand the men down and send them home. This is not a fight worth their lives.
